categories: [R, Python, Reticulate]
---

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(reticulate)
library(ggplot2)

# Point reticulate to project's virtual environment
use_virtualenv("../../.venv", required = TRUE)
```

## 1. Process Data in Python

```{python}
import pandas as pd

# Create a Python DataFrame
df_python = pd.DataFrame({
    'category': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'],
    'values': [10, 25, 15, 30]
})
```

## 2. Pass Python Object to R and Plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-reticulate-plot
#| fig-cap: "Data processed in Python and visualized with ggplot2 in R."

# Access the Python dataframe from R via the `py` object
df_r <- py$df_python

# Plot using ggplot2
ggplot(df_r, aes(x = category, y = values, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Data calculated in Python, plotted in R",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Values"
  )
```
